name: Disseminated Peritoneal Leiomyomatosis

criteria.description: Presence of multiple smooth muscle nodules scattered throughout the peritoneal surfaces
Histopathological confirmation of benign smooth muscle proliferation without atypia or malignancy
Exclusion of leiomyosarcoma or other malignant neoplasms by imaging and pathology
History or presence of uterine leiomyomas (fibroids)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple peritoneal nodules with histopathological confirmation of benign smooth muscle proliferation and exclusion of malignancy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires laparoscopic or surgical biopsy for definitive confirmation.

pathognomonic.notes: Palpable or visible nodules on peritoneal surfaces during surgery or imaging
searchTerms: multiple smooth muscle nodules in abdomen
peritoneal nodules made of muscle tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: Abdominal distension due to peritoneal nodules
searchTerms: abdominal bloating due to peritoneal masses
mass in pelvic area on imaging
pelvic tumor detected by ultrasound or MRI

occasional.symptomName: Urinary frequency or urgency due to pelvic mass effect
searchTerms: frequent or urgent urination from pelvic mass
bladder symptoms caused by pelvic tumor
urinary urgency due to mass effect

occasional.symptomName: Weight gain from ascites or mass effect
searchTerms: increased body weight due to ascites or mass

rare.symptomName: Intestinal obstruction secondary to nodular masses

rare.notes: Extremely rare but reported in literature
searchTerms: cancerous change in smooth muscle tumor
constitutional symptoms like fatigue and weight loss

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated CA-125 levels
imaging: Multiple peritoneal nodules on CT or MRI
Absence of invasive features or metastases
genetic: Some cases associated with hormonal receptor positivity (estrogen and progesterone receptors)
other: Histopathology showing benign smooth muscle proliferation without atypia
Immunohistochemistry positive for smooth muscle actin and desmin

distinguishingFeatures: Histopathological evidence of cellular atypia and mitotic activity
Presence of leiomyomatous nodules in lungs or other distant sites

redFlags: Rapid increase in size or number of peritoneal nodules
Onset of systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever
Histopathological signs of cellular atypia or malignancy
references: Nucci MR, et al. Disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis: a clinicopathologic study of 13 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2000.
Roberts ME, et al. Disseminated peritoneal leiomyomatosis: a review of the literature. Int J Gynecol Cancer. 2012.
